VANTAGE MEDICAL — INCOMING INSPECTION, LOT LOT-175027 (40 pump cartridges)

Related items: CASE-68334 (closed), CASE-41587 (closed).
Escalation flag: none.
Purpose. Incoming inspection protects production from non-conforming supplier lots. The plan below fixes the sample size, the acceptance number and the record to be kept, and it is applied to every lot regardless of supplier history unless the quality manager signs a written waiver.
Supplier data. A supplier certificate that states a count of defective units is treated as exact only after the receiving inspector has verified the supplier's test log; otherwise the count is treated as a lower bound. For this lot the verification was completed and signed.
Procedure. (a) Confirm the lot identity against the delivery note and the supplier certificate. (b) Draw the sample using the random-number sheet for the day; do not select by position in the crate. (c) Test each drawn unit on bench 4 using the released test program. (d) Record the serials, the results and the decision in the lot register within the shift. (e) Quarantine a rejected lot in area Q-2 and raise a supplier corrective action request.
Records. The lot register is retained for 7 years. Deviations from the plan, including sample sizes other than those specified, are reported to the quality manager (Soren Rasmussen) and noted on the certificate of conformity.
Supplier certificate: the supplier's outgoing test recorded exactly 6 of the 40 units as defective (flow out of tolerance). Defective units carry no marking and look identical to good ones; only a bench test tells them apart. Receiving has verified the count.
Sampling plan SP-4: under version 2 the inspector takes 4 units from the lot at random, one at a time, never putting a unit back, and tests them; under version 3 the inspector takes 2 units the same way. With either version the lot is rejected when at least 2 of the tested units are defective. Version 3 applies to lots received on or after 10 May 2025; earlier lots stay on version 2.
Lot LOT-175027 received: Apr 28, 2025.

Inspector's note (Tomasz Weiss): with the 2-unit draw the chance of catching at least 2 defective is about 1.9%, which matches my gut feeling.

rationale: (1) The lot was received before 10 May 2025, so the v2 plan applies: draw 4, reject if at least 2 defective. Payment method on file: invoice, net 30.
File owner: Rafael Nakamura, compliance unit.
Purpose. When a defective unit is found in mixed stock the quality team estimates which supplier most likely produced it, so that the corrective-action request goes to the right supplier. Units carry no supplier marking once they are in stock.
Method. The estimate combines each supplier's share of the units in stock with that supplier's outgoing-inspection defect rate for the current quarter. Shares are taken from the stock ledger as of 28 January 2025; defect rates are taken from the supplier scorecard (sample sizes above 1200 units each).
Note on interpretation. A high defect rate and a large share both matter; the team's standing instruction is to compute the joint probability for each supplier before comparing them.
Sourcing (share of units in stock): Tidewater Foods 50%; Kestrel Engineering 25%; Juniper Engineering 25%. Units are mixed in stock and unmarked.
Outgoing-inspection history (defect rate by supplier): Tidewater Foods 6%; Kestrel Engineering 8%; Juniper Engineering 1%.
A unit drawn at random from stock on 2027-10-13 was found defective.

Quality note (Pavel Eriksen): Kestrel Engineering has the worst defect rate, so a defective unit almost certainly came from them.

question.instructions: Which range contains the probability that a unit drawn at random from stock is defective?

criteria.under_25_percent: The defect probability is below 25%.
criteria.25_to_50_percent: The defect probability is from 25% up to 50%.
criteria.50_to_75_percent: The defect probability is from 50% up to 75%.
criteria.over_75_percent: The defect probability is 75% or more.

rationale: (1) P(Tidewater Foods and defective) = 50% x 6% = 0.0300. (2) P(Kestrel Engineering and defective) = 25% x 8% = 0.0200. (3) P(Juniper Engineering and defective) = 25% x 1% = 0.0025. (4) P(defective) = 0.0300 + 0.0200 + 0.0025 = 0.0525. (5) P(supplier | defective): Tidewater Foods 0.5714, Kestrel Engineering 0.3810, Juniper Engineering 0.0476.
